card.band: 8h. Frontier gets POSIX core fast and fails on strnum comparison, getline corner cases, printf and uninitialized variable rules, and the gawk extensions. A weaker model stops at the basic pattern-action loop. Interpreter subjects are medium-crowded, so the band is at most 3.
card.cheat: There is no awk binary in the image, and a wrapper around busybox is blocked by removing it. Hidden programs are not in the image, and many differ from the public tests.
card.grading: Hidden set: the remaining few hundred gawk test programs with expected stdout, plus generated programs diffed against real gawk run in the verifier only. Exact stdout and exit code; score is the fraction of cases passed.
card.reference: We take the goawk (MIT) base and extend it with the gawk features, about 3000 added lines. It passes the subset of cases that is graded.
card.source: https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gawk.git/tree/test @ savannah master 070138f; GPL-3.0-or-later (tests redistributable with source)
card.task: /app ships a sample of the test programs with .ok outputs and a build skeleton in Go or Rust. The agent builds an awk interpreter: the full POSIX grammar, getline forms, printf, regex, user functions, uninitialized and strnum semantics, plus gawk core extensions (gensub, patsplit, asort, PROCINFO sorted_in, BEGINFILE, length of arrays). It is run as `awk -f prog.awk input`.

spike_plan.kill_if: Removing awk alternatives breaks the image or cannot be sealed, or goawk unmodified already passes nearly all sampled gawk tests (frontier then reaches the reference trivially).
spike_plan.pass_if: Base image ships a usable awk that the image build can remove cleanly; goawk passes a substantial POSIX-core share but fails a clear gawk-extension share; outputs are deterministic across two runs.
steps: In a throwaway Debian trixie/bookworm container with network, run `ls -l /usr/bin/awk /etc/alternatives/awk` and `dpkg -l mawk original-awk gawk`; record what the base image really ships (confirms or kills the 'no awk in image' claim).
Clone gawk at commit 070138f from savannah; count test/*.awk and matching .ok files; confirm the total is in the 'few hundred' range.
Build gawk 5.3.x from source (or use the Debian package in the container) to generate reference outputs for a 50-test sample.
Build unmodified goawk at its current release; run it on the same 50-test sample against gawk .ok files to measure the POSIX-core pass rate and the gawk-extension pass rate.
Run the sample twice to check determinism (stdout and exit code).
Remove mawk and original-awk in the container and confirm no awk remains; verify the skeleton build still compiles without them.

v1.summary: The gawk test tree, GPL-3 licence and MIT goawk base check out, but the seed's claim that the image has no awk binary is contradicted: Debian's mawk is Priority required and is carried by minbase-style base images, so mawk must be removed and the wrapper path closed before acceptance. Not killed: the grading surface is large and sealable, the reference is a sizeable Go extension, and band 3 holds at E0 with a 60-minute spike to confirm the base image and goawk's pass rate.

v2.note: The gawk test/ tree and the goawk MIT base are confirmed; the pinned commit 070138f is not. The seed's 'no awk in image' claim is contradicted: Debian base images carry mawk (Priority required), so the image build must remove mawk, original-awk, busybox awk and the alternatives. The test set needs curation: exclude locale, --lint, debugger, bignum and stderr-wording tests so the grade covers only the stated scope. Generated programs diffed against gawk in the verifier give an open-ended surface. Buckets fall out naturally (POSIX core, getline, printf, strnum, each extension), and the horizon is long. Reference cost is the weak point: about 3000 added lines on goawk in 2-4 days is optimistic (K12 risk). Interpreters are medium-crowded, but awk is not on the crowded list.
